items.q: What should you remember about **Four brain areas, two jobs**?
items.a: **value assessment (worth pursuing?)** + action selection (go/no-go given current value).

items.q: What should you remember about **Three goal elements**?
items.a: **identify specific target; assess** progress; execute concrete action steps.

items.q: What should you remember about **Peripersonal = consume; extrapersonal = pursue**?
items.a: **progress evaluation happens in** peripersonal feeling-state; movement toward goals requires exteroceptive orientation.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vergence vs magnocellular vision**?
items.a: **narrow point focus → adrenaline,** systolic BP rise, goal-directed readiness; diffuse panoramic vision → relaxed, stay-in-place mode.

items.q: What should you remember about **Visualize failure, not success**?
items.a: **write/talk through specific negative** consequences of inaction; amygdala is built into goal circuitry.

items.q: What should you remember about **Moderate difficulty wins**?
items.a: **"maybe I can, maybe** I can't" doubles ongoing pursuit vs easy or impossible targets.

items.q: What should you remember about **Dopamine = motivation, not pleasure**?
items.a: **dopamine-depleted rats still enjoy** rewards but won't move one body-length to reach them.

items.q: What should you remember about **Reward prediction error**?
items.a: **biggest dopamine from unexpected positive events; anticipated** rewards pre-release dopamine then smaller peak at receipt; missed predictions → below-baseline drop (disappointment).

items.q: What should you remember about **Weekly check-ins**?
items.a: **tractable cadence to re-up** dopamine motivation when on track.

items.q: What should you remember about **Vision ↔ dopamine reciprocity**?
items.a: **narrow visual focus recruits** dopamine/epinephrine; raising dopamine sharpens outward visual targeting.

items.q: What should you remember about **Space-time bridging**?
items.a: **visual system batches time**: internal/near focus = fine time slices (breath/heartbeat clock); distant/broad focus = coarser future-oriented time framing; practice builds control over milestone + long-goal cognition.
